summary: Initial token delay observed on chat completions after allocator and model version bump
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (SynthAI Inc) reports elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests following a coordinated model version pin and runtime allocator change deployed on 2026-02-26. Increase is most visible at session start (first token) — streaming connection establishes but first token emission is delayed 600–1200ms above baseline.

Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible across multiple customer app sessions; affects ~4% of live traffic for this customer during peak windows.
- End-user experience: chat UI shows a long pause after "Connecting..." then a burst of tokens.
- No increase in 5xx rate observed; errors are rare (0.2%).

Environment:
- Hosted dedicated pool for SynthAI (dedicated tenant).
- Runtime rollout 2026-02-26 included allocator adjustments and compiler ABI patch: runtime v2.3.7 -> v2.4.0, allocator swap commit redwood-runtime/allocator#208.
- Models pinned: redwood/gptx-4-32k@v2026-02-25, fallback open/gpt-neox-20b@v2026-02-25.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a new chat session using SynthAI API key and model redwood/gptx-4-32k pinned.
2) Send single-turn prompt ~100 tokens of context (typical user prime).
3) Observe streaming handshake completes but first token arrives after 800–1100ms in affected cases.
4) Repeat across 10 sessions: 3–5 sessions show elevated TTFB.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming socket established (HTTP/2 SSE).
- "start" event emitted (server-side) but token emission delayed.
- KV cache warmup and later tokens stream at normal rate once generation starts.

Expected behavior:
- First token should appear within baseline SLO (<=150ms median for this tenant).

Logs & metrics collected:
- Grafana link (synthai-prod-ttfb): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/synthai/ttfb-2026-02-27
- Traces (Jaeger): trace IDs captured in comments.
- Sample request IDs: rQ-73a1f, rQ-73d4b, rQ-73f8c (attachments in ticket).
- Kernel allocator logs: /var/log/runtime/allocator/2026-02-26.log (snippet shows increased slab contention around 14:03 UTC).

Temporary workaround:
- Customer reverted model pin to previous model snapshot for a small % of traffic; observed TTFB returned to baseline for those sessions.
- Support applied a routing rule to prefer older runtime variant (v2.3.7) for SynthAI while investigation continues.

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: allocator change introduced a slow path on first KV cache allocation for long-context models.
- SRE observed correlation between elevated TTFB spikes and GC-like stalls in allocator logs.
- CPU and GPU metrics on affected hosts show no saturation; network egress stable.
- Scheduler traces show some requests waiting ~200–300ms in per-node work queue before being dispatched to the runtime process. Combined with allocator stall yields observed 800–1100ms delay.
- Related to INT-4189 where allocator churn was previously suspected during scale-up tests.

Next steps / open actions:
- Eng to reproduce locally with allocator debug flags (assigned to Diego).
- Eng to instrument allocator to emit per-allocation latency histogram (PR suggested redwood-runtime/allocator#210).
- SRE to temporarily route 20% traffic to pre-rollback runtime for comparison (in progress).
- CS to coordinate customer communication and confirm any additional examples.

Resolution status:
- Workarounds in place (routing to older runtime for subset). Root cause not yet confirmed.
